panels.name: Memory used by pod vs memory request
Limits by Container (2)
panels.markdownSource:
✅ If your container is hitting its limits and needs more resources:
  * 👉 Check if the nodes and namespaces have sufficient CPU and memory using the **[Pod Rightsizing & Capacity Optimization](#/dashboard-template/view.kubernetes.cluster.rightsizing)**
  * 👉 If both namespace and cluster have sufficient resources,  raise its limits to prevent potential problems.

panels.name: Requests by pod
panels.markdownSource: ⛳️ A **pod can be not ready** if the node in which it is running is out of resources and the node decides to evict the pod.  The higher the **resources versus requests** % a pod has, the higher the chances to be evicted by the node.

panels.name: New Panel (2)
panels.markdownSource: ⛳️ The **Golden Signals** (Errors, Latency, Traffic, and Saturation) give a good perspective of the performance of the application from the outside.

panels.name: New Panel (3)
panels.markdownSource: ✅ Check that the **Network Errors** and **HTTP Errors** are low or null.

panels.name: New Panel (4)
panels.markdownSource: ✅ Check that the **Latency** is under your SLO.

panels.name: New Panel (5)
panels.markdownSource: ✅ Check that the **Traffic** and **Request rate** are the expected values

panels.name: Limits by Container (3)
panels.markdownSource: ✅ Check the **containers using over 75% of the CPU and memory limits** in the panel. A container reaching its limits could cause *CPU throttling or out of memory kill* (OOM Kill).

panels.name: Requests by pod (2)
panels.markdownSource: ✅ If you want to rise the requests of the containers see the **[Pod Rightsizing & Capacity Optimization](#/dashboard-template/view.kubernetes.cluster.rightsizing) dashboard to adjust the requests** to check nodes and namespace capacity and adjust the requests.
